findings.location: procedure B20 (basis, date_rule, member test); md (a) M4 consequences and (c) item 9; sources S-MBA1947
findings.claim: The 1947 Military Bases Agreement 'retains only the use of the bases in the Philippines listed in Annex A (and Annex B on necessity)'; the surrender reached Army reservations on July 4, 1946; every non-listed reservation ended no later than 1947-03-26.
findings.evidence: Article XXI of the agreement (43 U.N.T.S. No. 673, UNTS copy at the doctrine's own URL) provides in para. 1 that 'the United States shall retain the right to occupy temporary quarters and installations now existing outside the bases mentioned in Annex A and Annex B, for such reasonable time, not exceeding two years', extendable by agreement (not for Manila) up to three years, and in para. 2 that 'the Port of Manila reservation with boundaries as of 1941 will be available for use to the United States armed forces until such time as other arrangements can be made'. So U.S. forces still held Army installations outside the listed bases after July 4, 1946, and the agreement itself kept the Port of Manila reservation in U.S. use after March 26, 1947. B20 members that set up or enlarged the Manila Port Reservation (EO 348A, EO 1298, EO 2838, EO 3344, EO 3500, and probably EO 5736, reclaimed blocks in Manila Harbor) are decided no by 1947-03-26 against the words of the source the branch cites. The doctrine's B20r reasoning (use retained by agreement keeps the member open) applies equally to them.
findings.fix: Cite Article XXI; move the Port Reservation members to an open branch (instrument that ended the Article XXI(2) availability not held); state that the July 4, 1946 date for Army reservations does not hold for installations kept as temporary quarters, and either raise the B20 upper bound to the latest date Article XXI(1) allows (March 26, 1950 on the three-year reading, March 26, 1949 for quarters in the City of Manila) or keep the 1947 bound only for members shown not to have been occupied under Article XXI.

findings.location: md (a) M4 consequences; JSON B20 gap 2; S-MBA1947 establishes
findings.claim: Note V 'reserved "adjustment of U.S. rights and titles to real property" for later settlement', a property question only; naval reservations at non-retained places were surrendered no later than 1947-03-26.
findings.evidence: The U.S. note (Exchange of Notes V, UNTS copy) says 'the question of the adjustment of any rights and titles held by the United States to real property in any of the bases covered by the aforementioned Agreement or any naval reservations or fueling stations not so covered is reserved' and 'will be settled subsequently in accordance with the terms of the Acts and Joint Resolution'. With sec. 10(b) of the 1934 Act ('shall remain in its present status' pending settlement), this expressly held over naval reservations outside the bases; the doctrine's quotation omits those words. No B20 member's summary names a naval reservation, so the effect on current leads is small, but the stated rule is unsupported.
findings.fix: Quote Note V in full and state that non-retained naval reservations are open pending the settlement Note V reserves, not ended by 1947-03-26.

summary: The doctrine's structure follows the coordinator rulings, and most citations check out: every held file's sha256 and pin match, and 24 of the 25 C-branch dates match the later orders' held texts. Six errors need fixing before adoption. Proclamation 2695 is cited at 60 Stat. 1325 when the held page and the URL show 1352. C22 dates EO 9293 to 1942-01-02 when the order is dated January 2, 1943. The doctrine says the engine reports no contradictions, but the engine flags 23. The doctrine also ignores held revocation edges that name 14 B33 members by number (Public Land Orders, 1943-1971), and it misses that member EO 432 placed EO 330A's reservation wholly under Interior. It offers EO 1450 as a possibly surviving reservation although a held edge shows PLO 833 revoked it in 1952. The most serious substantive error is in B20. Article XXI of the 1947 Military Bases Agreement, the source the branch itself relies on, kept the Port of Manila reservation and temporary installations outside the listed bases in U.S. use after March 26, 1947. The five or six Manila Port Reservation members are therefore wrongly decided no, and the July 4, 1946 and March 26, 1947 dates are unsupported for any installation kept under that article. The doctrine also quotes Note V of the agreement only in part; the omitted words reserve the question of naval reservations outside the bases. The minor items are narrow screen misses (EO 3402, EO 5157, EO 1397), the P2 dating of EO 5174 and EO 456, year-only lead dates, a misclassified Alaska member (EO 1920), and citation tidying. The open branches and the out-of-family routing are otherwise stated truthfully.
